messages:
emma: tiny support ask — trying to push ruby gem 0.13.0 but `gem push` errors with checksum mismatch on ci when using `rake release`. Anyone seen this on GH actions runner?

ryan: hm, we've seen failures when the `gemspec` has a different summary/description vs the built .gem. Are you building locally or in CI?

emma: CI. build step uses `bundle exec rake build` then `rake release` which calls `gem push`. Logs show `ERROR:  Gem::Package::FormatError - checksum mismatch for file lib/redwood.rake` inside the gem.

oliver: checksum mismatch often means files changed between build and push, or something mangled the gem during tar. Are you zipping artifacts or re-checking out workspace?

emma: workflow does a separate checkout in a later job for release (checkout@v3 with fetch-depth: 0). Could that change line endings? repo uses `.gitattributes` to enforce lf.

claire: also make sure the built gem isn't modified by the `artifact` upload/download step. We've had runners that accidentally expanded and recompressed leading to different checksum. Can you try building and pushing in the same job to isolate?

emma: good call. i'll try a single-job release. Quick question: we still sign gems with `gem signin`? I thought we moved to GPG-less flow and used `rubygems API key` in secrets.

ryan: we migrated to API key in CI last year. no GPG signing in CI anymore. release job should just `gem push --key RUBYGEMS_API_KEY` or use `gem push` after `echo $RUBYGEMS_API_KEY > ~/.gem/credentials` with perms 0600.

oliver: another angle — did your `.gemspec` include `spec.files = Dir[...]` that captures generated files? Generated docs or compiled extensions can vary and cause mismatch. Prefer explicit file list or regenerate before push.

emma: spec.files uses `git ls-files` so generated files shouldn't be included. I rebuilt in same job and push succeeded. So likely artifact roundtrip was the issue. I'll update the workflow to run build+push in same job.

claire: small follow-up: could we add a short note to the CONTRIBUTING or release guide about "avoid multi-job gem push"? New maintainers keep tripping over this.

emma: yes i'll submit a tiny PR to docs. Also: release-bot failed to post the release note because tag was `v0.13.0-beta` — the bot only looks for semver without pre-release.

release-bot: release-bot: release not created because tag matches pre-release. To force create a draft release add `--draft` to `gh release create` or update CI to call `gh release create v0.13.0-beta --prerelease`. See docs.

ryan: we could make the bot smarter but for now update the workflow to pass `--prerelease` when tag contains `-`. Also add a step to normalize tag name for stable releases.

oliver: last maintenance note: we're still shipping `vendor/cache` in the gem build for some folks which bloats the gem. Recommend adding `Gem::PackageTask` ignore or update `.gemspec` to exclude `vendor/cache`. Tiny PR incoming.

claire: yes please. Also check platform-specific extensions — CI on windows complained about `rake-compiler` missing during native extension build for `ffi` when testing older rubies. We had similar conversation last sprint.

emma: thanks all, PRs planned: 1) update workflow to single-job gem push and pass prerelease flag, 2) docs note in CONTRIBUTING, 3) cleanup gemspec excludes. Will tag reviewers shortly.

release-bot: workflow suggestion: use `actions/create-release` with `prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref, '-') }}` to auto-detect prerelease.

ryan: perfect. when PRs land can we do a patch release and ping CS? a few new maintainers hit this today.

emma: will do. merging after one LGTM. :+1:
